rationale: The literature confirms that pathogenic heterozygous variants in KDM2B (particularly within the CxxC zinc-finger domain) cause a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay/intellectual disability, congenital heart defects (e.g., ASD, VSD), structural ocular anomalies (such as coloboma and myopic astigmatism), and renal/urogenital malformations (such as renal agenesis/dysplasia). This triad significantly overlaps with the multi-system presentations of CHARGE syndrome (coloboma, heart anomalies, genitourinary defects) and Kabuki syndrome (cardiac, renal, and ocular anomalies). However, the specific claim that the absence of choanal atresia, semicircular canal agenesis, and persistent fetal finger pads reliably disfavors CHARGE/Kabuki to allow clinical diagnosis of KDM2B from phenotype alone is unsupported and conflicted: facial dysmorphisms in KDM2B are described as subtle rather than distinctive, classic syndromic features of CHARGE and Kabuki can also be incomplete in atypical cases, and available cohorts lack systematic negative reporting for inner-ear canal anatomy or choanal patency, necessitating molecular confirmation and peripheral blood DNA episignature testing for definitive differentiation.

evidence.text: Heterozygous pathogenic variants in KDM2B, with a mutational hotspot in the CxxC domain, present with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, congenital anomalies primarily of the heart, eyes, and urogenital system, and subtle facial dysmorphism.

source.title: Variants in the CxxC domain of the epigenetic regulator KDM2B support its role in developmental eye anomalies
source.quote: By screening 706 families with developmental eye disorders, we identified two cases with KDM2B-CxxC variants, NM_032590.5:c.1841G>C;p.(Arg614Pro) and NM_032590.5:c.1880G>C;p.(Cys627Ser), both resulting in a characteristic KDM2B DNA episignature. Both individuals exhibited complex structural eye defects, with neurodevelopmental, cardiac and renal anomalies variably present.

evidence.text: Three pediatric patients with KDM2B CxxC domain variants presented with developmental delay, cardiac defects (atrial and ventricular septal defects), unilateral renal agenesis/solitary kidney, myopic astigmatism, feeding difficulties, and cutaneous signs (hemangiomas, hypertrichosis, atopic dermatitis).

source.title: KDM2B‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case‐Series Supporting the CxxC Domain Phenotype With Emphasis on Ocular and Dermatologic Features
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: We present three children with KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder, each with a heterozygous variant in the CxxC domain of KDM2B. Patient 1 is a 2-year-old boy with developmental delay, solitary kidney, atrial septal defect, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 2 is a 2-year-old girl with global developmental delay, hip dysplasia, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 3 is a 5-year-old girl with autism, developmental delay, atrial septal defect, and ventricular septal defect, hypertrichosis, atopic dermatitis, and myopic astigmatism.

evidence.text: Kabuki and CHARGE syndromes exhibit broad phenotypic variability across cardiac, renal, and ocular axes; differential diagnosis between these epigenetic disorders frequently requires molecular classification and DNA episignature profiling rather than clinical observation alone.

conflicts: No published KDM2B cohort has systematically assessed or reported negative findings for choanal atresia or semicircular canal agenesis (e.g., via temporal bone CT), precluding their use as validated negative diagnostic criteria.

The facial phenotype of KDM2B is described as 'subtle facial dysmorphism', lacking a pathognomonic gestalt that would enable clinicians to isolate KDM2B cases purely based on clinical inspection without DNA episignature or genomic sequencing.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of temporal bone inner-ear malformations (semicircular canal dysplasia) and posterior nasal airway patency in confirmed KDM2B-CxxC variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: High-resolution imaging in a multi-center KDM2B cohort would establish whether semicircular canal agenesis or choanal stenosis genuinely never occurs in KDM2B, testing its validity as a definitive negative discriminator against CHARGE syndrome.

new_directions.question_text: Can computational facial phenotyping and machine learning differentiate KDM2B-related dysmorphism from atypical Kabuki and CHARGE syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: Because KDM2B exhibits subtle facial features, 3D photogrammetry and deep gestalt analysis could detect sub-visual dysmorphic patterns distinguishing it from other chromatin-associated disorders.
